title: Bruno AC HVAC Calculation Source Matrix
jurisdictionBaseline: Texas statewide baseline with project-specific local AHJ precedence
copyrightPolicy: Metadata, implementation summaries, identifiers, and official links only. Copyrighted standards/manuals are not reproduced.

sources.title: Texas ACR adopted-code baseline
sources.applicability: HVAC/ACR work in Texas on or after 2026-09-01; local amendments still apply.
sources.source_authority: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
sources.summary: Texas updated ACR adopted references to the 2024 IRC, IMC, IFGC, and UMC effective September 1, 2026.

sources.title: Texas 2026 NEC baseline for HVAC electrical coordination
sources.applicability: Electrical work in Texas on or after 2026-09-01, subject to Texas modifications, equipment nameplate/listing, and local AHJ.
sources.source_authority: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
sources.summary: Texas adopted the 2026 NEC as the state electrical code effective September 1, 2026, with a limited Texas modification. Equipment-specific circuit sizing remains dependent on nameplate/OEM data and installation conditions.

sources.title: Texas statewide minimum energy code — one- and two-family residential
sources.applicability: Texas one- and two-family residential construction three stories or fewer above grade where a qualifying local code does not supersede the statewide minimum.
sources.section: Texas Building Energy Performance Standards — Single-family residential
sources.summary: SECO identifies 2015 IRC Chapter 11 as the statewide minimum energy-code baseline for qualifying one- and two-family residential construction; local jurisdictions may adopt qualifying amendments or more stringent codes.

sources.title: Texas statewide minimum energy code — commercial
sources.applicability: Texas commercial, industrial and other covered construction where a qualifying local code does not supersede the statewide minimum.
sources.section: Texas Building Energy Performance Standards — Commercial
sources.summary: SECO identifies the 2015 IECC as the statewide minimum energy-code baseline for covered commercial construction; local jurisdictions may adopt qualifying amendments or more stringent codes.

sources.title: Austin adopted technical-code baseline
sources.applicability: Projects within City of Austin jurisdiction; verify project address and current amendments/interpretations.
sources.summary: Austin lists the 2024 IECC, 2024 IRC, 2024 UMC and other 2024 technical codes, with the 2026 NEC effective September 1, 2026.

sources.title: Project-specific local AHJ amendments and interpretations
sources.applicability: Every project; resolve the actual city/county/AHJ and attach its source before treating local requirements as verified.
sources.summary: Local amendments and interpretations can change model-code application. The app intentionally stores no generic Austin link as the authoritative source for non-Austin work; the operator must attach the actual project AHJ source.

sources.title: Austin commercial heating and cooling load calculation
sources.applicability: Commercial projects in Austin installing new HVAC equipment.
sources.section: 2024 IECC C403.2.1; Commercial Mechanical Plan Review checklist item 13
sources.summary: Austin commercial review requires design heating/cooling loads using ANSI/ASHRAE/ACCA Standard 183 or an approved equivalent computational procedure.

sources.title: Austin commercial mechanical COMcheck / energy review
sources.applicability: Austin commercial projects with new HVAC equipment.
sources.summary: Austin commercial review calls for a Mechanical COMcheck for new HVAC units and verification of applicable efficiency requirements.

sources.title: Austin commercial duct layout documentation
sources.applicability: Austin commercial work installing new ductwork.
sources.summary: Austin commercial review requires a duct layout showing size, class, gauge, and register locations for newly installed ductwork.

sources.title: Austin commercial outside-air calculation
sources.applicability: Austin commercial projects where outside-air requirements apply.
sources.summary: Austin commercial review requires outside-air calculations demonstrating that minimum outside-air rates are accommodated by the HVAC equipment.

sources.title: Bruno transparent envelope load v1
sources.jurisdiction: internal calculation method; code applicability resolved separately
sources.applicability: When the Bruno transparent envelope load engine is used. This identifies the implemented algorithm and does not claim Manual J, Manual N, Standard 183, or code-compliance certification.
sources.section: project-load-engine.js / Bruno transparent envelope load v1
sources.summary: Internal transparent envelope/load arithmetic used by the app. Regulatory and methodology standards are separate provenance and are not implied by this method identifier.

sources.title: ACCA Manual J residential load calculation methodology
sources.jurisdiction: US residential methodology / project code applicability required
sources.applicability: Residential dwelling load calculations when the adopted code/design path calls for Manual J or an approved equivalent.
sources.summary: Manual J is ACCA's ANSI-recognized residential load-calculation standard. The app must not claim Manual J compliance unless its implemented method is validated to that standard.

sources.title: ACCA Manual S residential equipment selection
sources.jurisdiction: US residential methodology / project code applicability required
sources.applicability: Residential equipment selection after a valid heating/cooling load is available when Manual S is the selected and verified policy source.
sources.section: ANSI/ACCA Manual S equipment-selection landing page
sources.summary: Manual S selects residential equipment using heating/cooling loads, manufacturer performance data, and design conditions. The runtime result cites this source only when the verified selection policy explicitly identifies it.

sources.title: ACCA Manual D residential duct design methodology
sources.jurisdiction: US residential methodology / project code applicability required
sources.applicability: Residential duct design after design airflow/equipment data are available where Manual D or equivalent is required/selected.
sources.summary: Manual D is an ANSI-recognized residential duct-design methodology using airflow, system geometry, fittings, duct materials, pressure losses, and blower performance.

sources.title: Selected equipment OEM installation / nameplate data
sources.applicability: Any output depending on exact equipment model, listing, rated capacity, voltage, phase, MCA, MOCP, line-set limits, accessories, refrigerant charge, controls, or installation instructions.
sources.section: Project-specific OEM document and equipment label
sources.summary: The calculator must remain unresolved for equipment-specific values until an exact model/nameplate/OEM source is attached. It must never infer MCA/MOCP, line-set diameter, charge, voltage, phase, or rated performance from tonnage alone.

sources.title: Austin A2L refrigerant interpretation
sources.applicability: Austin projects using A2L refrigerants where the interpretation is applicable to the selected system/install conditions.
sources.summary: Austin's interpretation library lists PM2024-0004 for A2L refrigerants. The exact interpretation document must be reviewed for project-specific application.
